terms.gloss: the top of, the surface of
terms.grammar: adjective, with the noun: summa aqua, the surface of the water
evidence: Plaut. Cas. 2.6.33: in aquā summā natāre (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fin. 4.64: ad aquam summam appropinquāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin says “the top water” as it says “the top of the mountain” (summus mōns): the adjective agrees with the thing. As a noun, summum is the top or surface (ā summō, Cic. Fin. 3.48). Its other senses are highest, greatest, last (Lewis & Short).
A post-Augustan word in this sense (Columella, Pliny): the surface of water, of a stone, a shell. In Cicero and the jurists it is a building on another man’s land (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quī dēmersī sunt in aquā … sī nōn longē absunt ā summō
phrases.english: those who have gone under the water, if they are not far from the surface
and thorns had covered its surface

sources: Lewis & Short: summus · Lewis & Short: superficies
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-vulgata), checked against the editions named there. Plautus and Cicero as Lewis & Short quotes them (s.v. superus).
